flashcards.front: What is a key advantage of Raspberry Pi over Arduino in terms of processing power?
flashcards.back: Raspberry Pi is more powerful in computation or processing power.

flashcards.front: How does Raspberry Pi's memory capacity compare to Arduino's?
flashcards.back: Raspberry Pi has better memory capacity.

flashcards.front: For what type of sensors is Raspberry Pi particularly attractive due to its processing capabilities?
flashcards.back: Sensors which require more processing, for example, imaging sensors and multimedia sensors.

flashcards.front: What is a significant trade-off when choosing Raspberry Pi over Arduino, besides power consumption?
flashcards.back: The cost of purchasing Raspberry Pi is generally more than the cost of Arduino.

flashcards.front: In an IoT application, when would Raspberry Pi be a better option than Arduino for a node?
flashcards.back: If the requirement is for the node to act as a server.

flashcards.front: What is Raspberry Pi commonly described as in simple terms?
flashcards.back: A micro-sized computer or a 'computer in your palm'.

flashcards.front: What specific type of computer is Raspberry Pi classified as?
flashcards.back: A single board computer (SBC).

flashcards.front: Name two reasons why Raspberry Pi has become popular for IoT and hobby electronics.
flashcards.back: It is a very low-cost device and very easy to access.

flashcards.front: What is the newest common variant of Raspberry Pi mentioned in the lecture?
flashcards.back: Raspberry Pi 3 Model B.

flashcards.front: What is the RAM capacity of Raspberry Pi 3 Model B and Pi 2 Model B?
flashcards.back: Both have 1 GB RAM.

flashcards.front: What is the RAM capacity of Raspberry Pi Zero?
What is the CPU type and approximate processing speed of Raspberry Pi 3 Model B?
flashcards.back: Quad-core Cortex A53 processor, approximately 1.2 GHz.

flashcards.front: Which common Raspberry Pi variant lacks built-in Ethernet and WiFi?
flashcards.back: Raspberry Pi Zero.

flashcards.front: What is the primary video output port on a Raspberry Pi?
flashcards.back: HDMI port.

flashcards.front: What do the initials GPIO stand for in the context of Raspberry Pi?
flashcards.back: General Purpose Input Output pins.

flashcards.front: How many GPIO pins are typically available on a Raspberry Pi?
flashcards.back: 40 GPIO pins.

flashcards.front: What is the main function of the memory card in a Raspberry Pi?
flashcards.back: It actually holds the OS (Operating System) of the Raspberry Pi.

flashcards.front: Name three types of physical ports found on a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B.
flashcards.back: HDMI port, USB ports, Ethernet port, Power adapter port, Sound card output. (Any three)

flashcards.front: What dual function can Raspberry Pi GPIO pins serve?
flashcards.back: They can act as both digital output and digital input.

flashcards.front: What are the basic components required for the initial setup of a Raspberry Pi?
flashcards.back: External monitor, HDMI cable, keyboard and mouse, 5V adapter, LAN cable, and a memory card with the OS.

flashcards.front: Name two official operating system distributions for Raspberry Pi.
flashcards.back: Raspbian and NOOBS.

flashcards.front: What software is recommended for writing a Raspbian image onto an SD card on a Windows system?
flashcards.back: Win32 Disk Imager.

flashcards.front: What is the default username and password for remotely logging into a Raspberry Pi system?
flashcards.back: Username: pi, Password: raspberry.

flashcards.front: What command is used to check the IP address of the Raspberry Pi from its terminal?
flashcards.back: ip config.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of the 'Expand File System' option in the Raspberry Pi configuration?
flashcards.back: To expand the compressed OS image to cover the maximum capacity of the memory card, providing more space.

flashcards.front: What does SSH stand for, and why is it enabled on Raspberry Pi?
flashcards.back: Secure Shell login; it allows remote access to the Raspberry Pi over the network from any remote PC.

flashcards.front: Name three programming languages that come pre-installed or are easily usable with Raspberry Pi.
flashcards.back: Python (2/3), Scratch, BlueJ (Java), C, C++, Ruby. (Any three)

flashcards.front: List two popular applications of Raspberry Pi in home environments.
flashcards.back: Home automation systems and home monitoring (as a lightweight web server for IoT).

flashcards.front: How can a Raspberry Pi be used as a lightweight web server for IoT?
flashcards.back: It can act as a server for IoT devices to upload data, and can run various analytics on that data.

flashcards.front: What is a key difference in power consumption between Raspberry Pi and Arduino?
flashcards.back: Raspberry Pi has more power consumption compared to Arduino due to its higher computation capabilities.
